u8-l01.title: The active king
u8-l01.summary: In the endgame, the king attacks too

u8-l01-s01.text: In the endgame there are hardly any pieces left to give mate, and the king becomes an attacking piece. Here the black king marches to f4: from there it attacks the g4 pawn, and the white king is too far away to defend it.

u8-l01-s02.text: The same here: the black king heads for f5 and attacks the g5 pawn. The white king cannot defend it and Black eats it.

u8-l01-s03.prompt: White to move. What does the king do to win the a6 pawn?
options: It goes to b6 and attacks it
It goes to d5, toward the center
It goes to b7 and moves away from the pawn
u8-l01-s03.explanation: With Kb6 the king attacks the a6 pawn and the black king can't get there in time to defend it.
feedback: Going to the center wins nothing: the a6 pawn is right next to your king.
Moving away from the pawn is the opposite of what you need.

u8-l01-s04.prompt: Tap the square the black king must go to in order to attack the g5 pawn.
u8-l01-s04.hint: It has to end up next to the pawn, on a square the white king can't watch.

u8-l01-s05.prompt: Attack the a6 pawn with the king.
u8-l01-s05.hint: The white king can stand next to the pawn. The black king can't get there to defend it.
u8-l01-s05.success: Correct. Kb6 attacks the pawn and the enemy king can't defend it.

u8-l01-s06.prompt: Capture the a2 pawn with the king.
u8-l01-s06.hint: The a2 pawn is right next to your king and nobody defends it.
u8-l01-s06.success: Correct. Kxa2 wins the pawn and clears the way for the a-pawn.

u8-l01-s07.prompt: Attack the b7 pawn with the king.
u8-l01-s07.hint: Your king can go around the black king and attack the pawn from another square.
u8-l01-s07.success: Correct. Kc7 attacks the b7 pawn and the black king can't defend it.

u8-l01-s08.success: Well solved: this position comes from a real game.
u8-l01-s08.hint: Take the king toward the enemy pawns: don't stay at home.

u8-l01-s09.success: Well solved: this position comes from a real game.
u8-l01-s09.hint: Take the king toward the enemy pawns: don't stay at home.

u8-l02.title: The distant passed pawn
u8-l02.summary: A pawn far from the enemy king

u8-l02-s01.text: White has a passed pawn on the h-file, far from the black king, which is at the other end. With h5 the race begins: both sides queen, but White gets there first and its new queen, with checks, stops the black pawn.

u8-l02-s02.text: Here Black's passed pawn is on the a-file, far from the white king. It queens and nobody can stop it, and the white pawns arrive too late.

u8-l02-s03.prompt: White to move. What is best?
options: Push the h-pawn, which is far from the black king
Take the king toward the pawns on the a-file
u8-l02-s03.explanation: The black king is at the other end and can't stop the h-pawn. Pushing it wins the race.
feedback: With the king far from the h-pawn, what matters most is that the pawn runs.
The g-pawn doesn't have the same advantage: it is closer to the enemy king.

u8-l02-s04.prompt: Tap the passed pawn that is farthest from the black king.
u8-l02-s04.hint: It's the pawn at the edge of the board, opposite the black king's position.

u8-l02-s05.prompt: Push the pawn that is far from the enemy king.
u8-l02-s05.hint: Nothing can stop the h-pawn: the black king is on the other side.
u8-l02-s05.success: Correct. h5 starts the race: the pawn queens and the black king arrives too late.

u8-l02-s06.prompt: Push the pawn that is far from the enemy king.
u8-l02-s06.hint: The a-pawn queens before the white king can do anything.
u8-l02-s06.success: Correct. a4 starts the race: the pawn queens and the white king arrives too late.

u8-l02-s07.success: Well solved: this position comes from a real game.
u8-l02-s07.hint: Look for the pawn that is farthest from the enemy king and push it.

u8-l02-s08.success: Well solved: this position comes from a real game.
u8-l02-s08.hint: Look for the pawn that is farthest from the enemy king and push it.

u8-l02-s09.text: Summary: a passed pawn far from the enemy king is a double-edged weapon. Either it queens, or the enemy king has to chase it and leaves its other pawns alone. Those are the two weaknesses: the passed pawn and the pawns left unprotected.

u8-l03.title: Queen against pawn
u8-l03.summary: When the pawn is one step from queening

u8-l03-s01.text: The white queen controls d1 from a4: if the pawn queens, the queen captures it with check. Meanwhile the white king comes closer and, together, they finish off the pawn and the king.

u8-l03-s02.text: By contrast, with a rook pawn on the seventh and the black king near the corner, the queen cannot win. The black king takes refuge in the corner and any attempt ends in a draw by stalemate.

u8-l03-s03.prompt: Which of these pawns on the seventh is usually a draw against the queen?
options: The rook pawn, on the a-file
The central pawn, on the d-file
u8-l03-s03.explanation: With a rook pawn and the enemy king close, stalemate saves Black. With a central pawn, on the other hand, the queen wins.
feedback: With a central pawn the queen wins: the king doesn't have the corner to take refuge in.
With the rook pawn and the king near the corner, the queen doesn't win.

u8-l03-s04.prompt: The black pawn wants to queen on d1. Tap the square the queen controls from a4.
u8-l03-s04.hint: Follow the queen's diagonal toward the bottom right corner.

u8-l03-s05.prompt: Win with the queen and king against the pawn and king. Stockfish defends.
u8-l03-s05.success: Correct. The queen stopped the pawn and you gave mate.
u8-l03-s05.hint: That move lets the win slip away. Keep the queen controlling the queening square and bring the king closer without stalemating.

u8-l03-s06.text: Summary: the queen controls the queening square and the king comes closer. Against a rook pawn on the seventh with the king near the corner, stalemate gives a draw.

u8-l04.title: The Philidor position
u8-l04.summary: The safe defense with the rook

u8-l04-s01.text: In the rook and pawn against rook ending, the safest defense is the Philidor position: the defending rook on the sixth rank and the king on the last rank, in front of the pawn. That way the enemy king and pawn can't advance.

u8-l04-s02.prompt: On which rank does the defending side place the rook?
options: On the sixth rank, the third from its own side
On the first rank, behind the pawn
u8-l04-s02.explanation: The rook on the sixth rank cuts off the king and the pawn: the enemy king can't advance to the sixth rank.
feedback: Behind the pawn works later, when the pawn has already reached the sixth rank. At the start, the rook goes on the sixth.
On the pawn's file the rook would be a target and wouldn't stop the enemy king.

u8-l04-s03.prompt: The black rook controls the sixth rank. Tap the two squares on that rank the white king or the pawn want to advance to.
u8-l04-s03.hint: They're in front of the white king and pawn, on the sixth rank.

u8-l04-s04.prompt: Defend the ending. Stockfish plays White and tries to win. Hold on for 30 moves without losing.
u8-l04-s04.success: Correct. You held for 30 moves: the Philidor position is a draw.
u8-l04-s04.hint: With that move White wins. Keep the rook on the sixth rank and the king on the last rank, in front of the pawn.

u8-l04-s05.text: Summary: rook on the sixth rank and king on the last. When the pawn reaches the sixth rank, the rook goes behind it and gives checks from a distance.

u8-l05.title: Cutting off the king with the rook

u8-l05-s01.text: The rook on c1 controls the c-file: the black king can't cross it and can't reach the b4 pawn. Meanwhile the pawn advances and nobody can stop it. That's cutting off the king with the rook.

u8-l05-s02.prompt: Tap the three squares on the c-file the black king could use to cross to the other half of the board.
u8-l05-s02.hint: They're the squares on the c-file next to the black king.

u8-l05-s03.prompt: Why can't the black king get close to the pawn?
options: The rook controls the c-file and blocks its way
The pawn is protected by the rook
u8-l05-s03.explanation: To reach the pawn, the black king would have to cross the c-file, and the rook watches all of it.
feedback: The white king is far from the black king: what blocks its way is the rook.
The rook doesn't protect the b4 pawn: what it does is cut off the file.

u8-l05-s04.text: You can also cut off by ranks. With Rh5 the rook controls the 5th rank: the black king cannot go down and the b4 pawn advances calmly.

u8-l05-s05.prompt: Queen the pawn without losing the new queen. Stockfish defends.
u8-l05-s05.success: Correct. The rook cut off the king and the pawn queened.
u8-l05-s05.hint: That move lets the win slip away. Keep the rook on the c-file and advance the pawn.

u8-l05-s06.prompt: Cut off the king with the rook and queen the pawn. Stockfish defends.
u8-l05-s06.success: Correct. You cut off the king and the pawn queened.
u8-l05-s06.hint: That move lets the win slip away. Put the rook on a rank or file the black king can't cross.

u8-l05-s07.text: Summary: the rook cuts off the king along a file or rank it can't cross. With the king cut off, the pawn advances on its own.

u8-l06-s01.text: With opposite-colored bishops, each bishop controls squares the other can't attack. The defending bishop stops the pawn and the king takes shelter behind it. That's why an extra pawn is usually not enough to win.

u8-l06-s02.prompt: A bishop only attacks squares of its own color. Which squares can't the black bishop attack, since it goes on light squares?
u8-l06-s02.explanation: The black bishop on f1 goes on light squares. The f4 pawn is on a dark square: that bishop can never attack it.
feedback: It can attack the light ones: they are its own.
Each bishop has its own color and can't change it.

u8-l06-s03.prompt: Tap the white pawn the black bishop can never attack.
u8-l06-s03.hint: It's the pawn on a square of a different color from your bishop.

u8-l06-s04.prompt: Defend the ending. Stockfish plays White and tries to win. Hold on for 20 moves without losing.
u8-l06-s04.success: Correct. You held for 20 moves: with opposite-colored bishops, being a pawn down does not lose.
u8-l06-s04.hint: With that move White wins. Keep the king close and leave the bishop on a long diagonal that stops the pawn.

u8-l06-s05.text: Summary: with opposite-colored bishops, each attacks squares the other doesn't touch, and the side a pawn down can hold on.

u8-l07.title: Bishop versus Knight
u8-l07.summary: Each piece shines in a different position

u8-l07-s01.text: In the endgame, the bishop and the knight are worth almost the same, but they are not used for the same thing. The bishop on c1 reaches both wings in a few moves; the knight on f6 only reaches nearby squares.

u8-l07-s02.text: Here the knight on d5 dominates the center and has a strong square. The bishop on c1, on the other hand, has little space: its pawns on b2 and c3 close off the queen's flank. With the fixed structure, the knight is the best piece.

u8-l07-s03.prompt: With pawns on both flanks, which piece is usually more comfortable?
u8-l07-s03.explanation: The bishop crosses the board in one move and covers both wings. The knight needs several moves to change flanks.
feedback: The knight is strong near the center, but it takes time to get from one wing to another.
It's not the same: the pawn structure decides which piece is worth more.

u8-l07-s04.prompt: The black pawn is one step away from promotion. Save the game.
u8-l07-s04.hint: The knight can capture the pawn from d3. After capturing it, king and knight against king are not enough to checkmate.
u8-l07-s04.success: Correct. Nxb2 eliminates the pawn and the game ends in a draw due to lack of material.

u8-l07-s05.prompt: After capturing the pawn, how does the game end?
u8-l07-s05.explanation: King and knight against king cannot checkmate. The game is a draw.
options: It's a draw due to lack of material
feedback: With only one knight, checkmate cannot be forced.
The black king also cannot win: there is no material left to attack.

u8-l07-s06.prompt: Touch the square of the black knight that dominates the center.
u8-l07-s06.hint: It is on a central square from which it attacks several points.

u8-l07-s07.text: Summary: the bishop is better with pawns on both flanks; the knight, with a strong square and fixed pawns. And if the opponent has a pawn about to promote, giving the piece for that pawn can save half a point.

u8-l08.title: The Two Weaknesses
u8-l08.summary: Attack one to win on the other

u8-l08-s01.text: The pawns on a4 and h4 are passed and separated. The black king can only go after one: if it goes to the queen side, the h4 pawn runs towards promotion.

u8-l08-s02.text: The same happens with the pieces: black has to defend a7 and h7. Your rook attacks a7; if the black rook goes to defend it, you switch to h7. One piece cannot cover two weaknesses at once.

u8-l08-s03.prompt: What do you do when the opponent has two weaknesses?
u8-l08-s03.explanation: If the opponent defends one weakness, the other is left unprotected. The key is to force them to choose.
options: Attack one so the opponent moves away and win on the other
feedback: Changing pieces does not create new weaknesses.
Defending does not win: you must attack the opponent's weakness.

u8-l08-s04.prompt: Advance a passed pawn so the black king cannot reach both.
u8-l08-s04.hint: Either of the two pawns is far from the black king. Choose one and run.
u8-l08-s04.success: Correct. The black king cannot cover both flanks: one of the pawns will promote.

u8-l08-s05.prompt: Tap the two passed white pawns.
u8-l08-s05.hint: They are the pawns on the two flanks, with no opposing pawns in front.

u8-l08-s06.text: Summary: one weakness is defended; two weaknesses are not. Attack one so the opponent moves away and you win on the other. In pawn endgames, two passed pawns on opposite flanks win for the same reason.
